correctness.rationale: The proof was reconstructed directly. For a nonempty complement \(T\), restrained domination requires \(T\) to meet both bipartition sides. Let \(a\) be the least \(A\)-class met by \(T\) and \(b\) the greatest \(B\)-class met by \(T\). Nesting of neighborhoods makes the condition on every \(T\cap A\) vertex equivalent to the prefix \(B_1\cup\cdots\cup B_a\) containing at least one vertex of \(T\) and at least one of \(S\); dually, every \(T\cap B\) vertex is handled exactly by the corresponding suffix \(A_b\cup\cdots\cup A_p\). These are necessary and sufficient. Once \((a,b)\) is fixed, the two side choices are independent and the three relative-order cases \(b<a\), \(b=a\), \(a<b\) give exactly the stated \(E_m\) and \(P_m\) factors without double counting. I independently replayed exhaustive definition-versus-formula checking for all canonical profiles with \(p\le4\), class sizes in \(\{1,2,3\}\), and total order at most 11: 540 profiles and 687,124 subsets with no mismatch. The finite replay is supplementary only.
correctness.risk: The formula assumes connected chain graphs in the stated canonical nesting orientation.

value.rationale: The result upgrades a known minimum-optimization problem to a complete structural classification and full polynomial for a natural hereditary bipartite class. The prefix/suffix boundary description is reusable, and the formula gives every cardinality count, the minimum, and the number of minimum sets. This is a natural complete enumerative classification rather than an isolated coefficient.
value.risk: The expression is a double sum rather than a simpler factorization and is specific to chain graphs.

final_claim: For every finite connected chain graph in canonical twin classes \(A_1,\ldots,A_p,B_1,\ldots,B_p\) with \(A_i\) adjacent to \(B_j\) exactly when \(j\le i\), complements of restrained dominating sets are classified by a unique pair of extremal indices \((a,b)\) and two nonempty-proper prefix/suffix conditions. This yields the exact double-sum complement enumerator \(Q_G(y)\) and therefore the full restrained domination polynomial \(D_r(G;x)=x^NQ_G(x^{-1})\), including the minimum number and count as consequences.
